text: When you were five, one summer lasted forever.
Now a whole year slips by between two birthdays.
Here's one idea. At five, a year is a fifth of your whole life.
At fifty, it's one fiftieth. Each year is a smaller slice.
But there's a stranger reason. Your brain doesn't keep a clock. It keeps memories.
A first day at school. The first time you saw the sea. New things leave marks.
Routine leaves almost none. A hundred mornings fold into one.
So looking back, a year without new memories feels short.
The fix? Do something new. Go somewhere. Learn something.
Fill the page, and the year gets longer again.
